title: Angels, Demons, Trajectory, Topology and Spin
purpose: Deepen the Tree of Life / Tree of Strife research by coupling comparative angelology and demonology to a disciplined study of trajectory, topology, quantum fields, the Standard Model and spin. Similarities are explicitly analogical, not claims that supernatural beings are physical particles.
epistemic_rule: Keep historical-religious claims, mathematical/physical claims and Potatoverse interpretation separate.

nodes.name: Angels
nodes.description: Comparative category for angelic and intermediary beings; meanings vary by tradition and period.

nodes.name: Demons
nodes.description: Comparative category for demons, harmful spirits and adversarial beings; taxonomies vary by tradition and period.

nodes.name: Angelology
nodes.description: Study of angelic beings, hierarchies, functions, names and representations.

nodes.name: Demonology
nodes.description: Study of demons, adversarial spirits, possession, protection, exorcism and related traditions.

nodes.name: Mal'akh / Messenger
nodes.description: Hebrew messenger term; angelic interpretation depends on textual context.

nodes.name: Michael
nodes.description: Named heavenly defender figure in Jewish and Christian traditions.

nodes.name: Gabriel
nodes.description: Named angel associated with revelation and interpretation in biblical and later traditions.

nodes.name: Raphael
nodes.description: Angel associated especially with healing in Tobit and later traditions.

nodes.name: Uriel
nodes.description: Heavenly figure prominent in some Second Temple and later Jewish and Christian traditions.

nodes.name: Samael
nodes.description: Complex figure whose roles vary across Jewish texts, including accusatory and adversarial dimensions; later Qliphothic systems add further correspondences.

nodes.name: Lilith
nodes.description: Figure developing from ancient Near Eastern night-spirit traditions through rabbinic and medieval Kabbalistic literature.

nodes.name: Ashmedai / Asmodeus
nodes.description: Demonic king figure with distinct portrayals in Tobit, rabbinic literature and later demonology.

nodes.name: Sitra Aḥra / Other Side
nodes.description: Kabbalistic language for the adversarial or other side in relation to holiness; not an equal dualistic god-principle.

nodes.name: Qelippot / Shells
nodes.description: Shells or husks associated with blockage, impurity and concealment of sparks.

nodes.name: Nitzotzot / Sparks
nodes.description: Holy sparks in Lurianic cosmology whose recovery participates in repair.

nodes.name: Tzimtzum
nodes.description: Lurianic contraction/withdrawal concept preceding differentiation and finite creation.

nodes.name: Shevirat ha-Kelim
nodes.description: Breaking of the vessels in Lurianic cosmology, producing a condition in which sparks become dispersed and concealed.

nodes.name: Birur
nodes.description: Clarification/extraction of sparks from mixed or broken conditions in Lurianic interpretation.

nodes.name: Tikkun
nodes.description: Repair/restoration process in Kabbalistic thought, especially Lurianic cosmology.

nodes.name: Trajectory
nodes.description: Evolutionary path through a state space; classical mechanics uses trajectories, while quantum theory generally does not assign a unique microscopic path between observations.

nodes.name: State Space
nodes.description: Space of possible states through which a system can evolve.

nodes.name: Topology
nodes.description: Study of properties preserved under continuous deformation, including connectivity, holes, boundaries and winding.

nodes.name: Configuration Space
nodes.description: Space of possible configurations; its topology can constrain exchange paths and quantum phases.

nodes.name: Gauge Field
nodes.description: Field structure underlying gauge interactions in quantum field theory.

nodes.name: Topological Charge
nodes.description: Quantity characterizing nontrivial global field configurations in relevant gauge theories.

nodes.name: Instantons
nodes.description: Finite-action Euclidean field configurations associated with nontrivial gauge-field topology and tunneling phenomena in relevant theories.

nodes.name: Standard Model
nodes.description: Quantum field theory of quarks, leptons, gauge bosons and the Higgs sector describing electromagnetic, weak and strong interactions.

nodes.name: Spin
nodes.description: Intrinsic quantum angular momentum represented through rotational/Lorentz symmetry; not literal classical spinning.

nodes.name: Fermion
nodes.description: Half-integer-spin particle class obeying fermionic statistics; Standard Model matter fields are fermionic.

nodes.name: Boson
nodes.description: Integer-spin particle class obeying bosonic statistics; Standard Model gauge carriers are bosonic.

nodes.name: Higgs Boson
nodes.description: Spin-0 elementary particle associated with the Higgs field.

nodes.name: Gauge Symmetry
nodes.description: Local symmetry structure underlying electromagnetic, weak and strong gauge interactions.

nodes.name: Quantum Path Integral
nodes.description: Formalism for calculating transition amplitudes by summing contributions associated with possible histories.

nodes.name: Helicity
nodes.description: Projection of spin along momentum, especially useful for massless or ultrarelativistic particles.
